target_customer: Independent writers and publishers who want to charge for newsletters, and readers who subscribe
problem: Writers lacked a simple way to run a paid email publication; Substack bundles newsletter, sign-up page, subscriptions and payments.
business_model: Take rate of 10 percent of paid subscriptions plus payment fees (per Poynter, March 2018)

founders.name: Chris Best
previous_startups: Kik (co-founder and CTO, per YC page)

founders.name: Hamish McKenzie
founders.background_notes: Described as co-founder and COO by Poynter (2018).

competitors.name: TinyLetter
competitors.what: Free email newsletter tool from Mailchimp without paid subscriptions
competitors.traction_then: Writers such as Helena Fitzgerald moved from it to Substack

technical_complexity.rationale: Email delivery, payments and publishing pages are standard web engineering for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Writers bring subscribers and the platform adds discovery, but exporting lists is possible so lock-in is moderate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Twitter bought Revue and Facebook and Forbes launched newsletter efforts per TechCrunch (March 2021); Substack kept growing.

market_need_then: In 2018 writers moved from free tools to paid email; Poynter reported Outside Magazine launching paid newsletters and writers calling it lucrative.

identity.logo: Orange S icon and wordmark; later bookmark-style mark
identity.visual_style: Warm editorial look with orange accent

branding.brand_signature: Signature orange and the idea of independent writers

rebrands.to: New logo described as a bookmark
rebrands.why: Not stated; Substack said actual designers made it

branding.community_and_virality: Substack has become a verb and a topic of commentary (Know Your Meme entry and Daring Fireball discussion appear in search results).

brand_strength.rationale: Widely recognized; the name is shorthand for paid independent newsletters and is also debated as a platform brand for writers.

outcome_analysis: Substack grew paid newsletters into a large platform, raised a 15.3 million dollar Series A in 2019, a 65 million dollar Series B at about 650 million in 2021 and a 100 million dollar Series C at 1.1 billion in 2025. It cut 14 percent of staff in mid-2022 but, per Sacra, reached positive cash flow in early 2025, supported by paid subscription growth to over 5 million.
notes: Series A amount, date and investors come from search results (TechCrunch, Fortune, Nieman Lab headlines), not opened pages. Series B valuation reported by Axios via TechCrunch; the lead was described as likely a16z. Series C valuation per NYT via TechCrunch. An early seed of about 2 million in 2018 appears only in one timeline, unverified. Revenue and cash flow figures from Sacra are third-party estimates. Education not found for founders.
